target: Jag tvättar mig och klär på mig.
english: I wash up and get dressed.
tip: Two reflexives in one sentence – each needs its own "mig."

english: I can't swim.
tip: Inte follows the modal verb in a main clause: kan inte simma. The negation sits right after kan.

english: I don't usually complain.
tip: brukar plus an infinitive means usually or tend to: Jag brukar klaga = I usually complain.

english: He laughs at the joke.
tip: Laugh at something is skratta åt, not på or till: skrattar åt skämtet = laughs at the joke.

english: I'm running around in the store.
tip: Swedish has no separate continuous form. springer means both I run and I am running.

english: The book is in the box.
tip: For things resting flat Swedish uses ligger, not är: Boken ligger i lådan = the book is in the box.

english: Actually, I like winter.
tip: Start a sentence with an adverb like Faktiskt and the verb comes before the subject: Faktiskt tycker jag.

english: I don't like it.
tip: Inte splits the particle verb tycka om: tycker inte om. The om belongs to the verb, not a preposition.

english: He hasn't even tried.
tip: inte ens means not even, and sits between har and försökt: har inte ens försökt.

english: Everywhere you see Swedish flags.
tip: man is a generic you or one, for people in general: ser man = you see, one sees.

english: We couldn't find the way.
tip: kunde is the past of kan (can): kunde inte hitta = couldn't find.

english: January is the coldest month.
tip: Superlatives take den plus the -aste form plus a definite noun: den kallaste månaden.

english: I didn't use to like it.
tip: brukade is the past of brukar and means used to: brukade inte gilla = didn't use to like.

english: Turn right at the traffic light.
tip: Commands use the plain verb form with no pronoun: Sväng = turn.

target: Fortfarande bor hon i samma stad.
english: She still lives in the same city.
tip: samma is followed by a plain noun with no definite ending: samma stad, not samma staden.

target: Jag hoppas att det inte regnar snart.
english: I hope it doesn't rain soon.
tip: hoppas always ends in -s even though it is active: Jag hoppas = I hope.

target: Ska vi ses imorgon nästa vecka nu?
english: Shall we meet tomorrow next week now?
tip: Yes or no questions start with the verb: Ska vi ses...? = Shall we meet...?

target: Jag kommer hem från jobbet på kvällen.
english: I get home from work in the evening.
tip: hem is home as a direction you move toward; hemma is home as a location: kommer hem = come home.

target: De köpte ett stort hus nära sjön.
english: They bought a big house near the lake.
tip: Adjectives add -t with ett-words: ett stort hus. On its own it would be stor.

target: Golvet är smutsigare än igår efter festen.
english: The floor is dirtier than yesterday after the party.
tip: Comparatives add -are and use än for than: smutsigare än igår = dirtier than yesterday.

target: Vädret idag är lika bra som igår.
english: The weather today is just as good as yesterday.
tip: For an equal comparison use lika plus adjective plus som: lika bra som = just as good as.

target: Hur vill du betala just nu snart?
english: How do you want to pay right now soon?
tip: Hur vill du betala: du works for everyone since the 1960s du-reform, strangers and bosses alike.

target: En fattig familj fick hjälp av sina grannar.
english: A poor family received help from their neighbors.
tip: sina means their own and points back to the subject of the clause: sina grannar = their own neighbors.

target: Jag hittade en mer intressant bok på biblioteket.
english: I found a more interesting book at the library.
tip: Longer adjectives form the comparative with mer, not -are: mer intressant = more interesting.

target: Troligen kommer det att snöa imorgon enligt prognosen.
english: Probably it will snow tomorrow according to the forecast.
tip: kommer att plus an infinitive is the future will: kommer att snöa = will snow.

target: Det är alltid roligt att lära känna nya människor här.
english: It is always fun to get to know new people here.
tip: A frequency adverb sits right after the verb in a main clause: är alltid roligt, with alltid following är.

english: The Lucia procession takes place in December.
tip: The -s ending makes a passive here: ses = is seen or takes place, from se (to see).

target: Dricksen ingår alltid i priset på den här restaurangen.
english: The tip is always included in the price at this restaurant.
tip: Tipping is not expected in Sweden – service charge is usually included.

english: It's more expensive.
tip: Comparatives usually add -are: dyr becomes dyrare (more expensive). No separate word for more is needed.

english: We'll meet on Monday.
tip: Ses is an s-verb meaning see each other. Vi ses is the everyday way to say see you later.
